prompt.alinti: You can now turn your computer into a tireless research assistant.
Imagine you have a tiny digital scientist living in your laptop that doesn't need to sleep or take breaks.
This new tool, called Open Research, has already grabbed 3,495 stars because it lets you hand off the boring parts of a project to an automated helper.
Think of it like hiring a dedicated intern who handles all your paperwork and organizes your messy notes while you focus on the big ideas.
It runs experiments on its own by testing different theories, writing down the results, and keeping every version of your work perfectly sorted in one place.
It works with the tools you might already use to write code, so it fits right into your current workflow without needing a complete overhaul.
You stay in total control. Since everything stays on your own machine, instead of being sent to some mysterious cloud.
check out the project on GitHub to see how it works.
Turn Claude Code, Codex, penCode, orCursor into research agents that can review literature, develop hypotheses, run experiments, and produce research artifacts.
Install the CLI on macOS or Linux, then launch OpenResearch.
On Windows, use the beta download above after installing Git for Windows.
orxup opens the local dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:4791.
Connect a local model to use LMStudio, Ollama, or custom endpoint with OpenCode.
Create an account at openresearch.sh to receive email updates and use managed OpenResearch compute.
